title: "Masked Language Model"
description: "A language model trained to predict tokens hidden or corrupted within an input sequence."
term: "Masked Language Model"
letter: "M"

difficulty: "Intermediate"

## Simple explanation

A masked language model learns by reading text with some words hidden and
trying to recover them. This encourages the model to use surrounding context
from both before and after the hidden word.

## Technical explanation

During masked language modeling, selected input tokens are replaced or
corrupted, and the model is trained to predict their original identities.
This is a form of self-supervised learning because the training targets come
from the text itself. BERT is a well-known model trained with a masked-token
objective.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Masked language modeling produces contextual representations useful for
classification, retrieval, and other language-understanding tasks. Its
bidirectional context makes the objective different from next-token
prediction, which is commonly used to train generative LLMs.

## How it works

The training pipeline selects positions to predict, constructs a corrupted
input, and computes a loss between the model's predicted token distribution
and the original tokens at those positions. Masking rules and the proportion
of selected tokens are part of the training recipe.

## Practical example

Given "The bird lives in a [MASK]," a masked language model may assign a high
probability to "nest." The model uses context on both sides of the masked
position when available.

## Common misconceptions

- Predicting a masked token is not the same objective as generating text one token at a time.
- A masked language model can provide useful representations without being designed for unrestricted text generation.
- The mask token and training corruption strategy are model-design choices, not universal requirements for every language model.
